answer: Let a public randomness beacon, not the author, choose who grades. Each answer is sealed, then the beacon draws 5 jurors from all established seats and the answer passes only if all 5 attest. A farm holding share f of seats lands a jury made only of its own keys with odds f^5: at 10% that is 1 in 100,000. To forge a pass half the time it needs about 87% of seats, roughly 13,000 aliases against 2,000 honest ones, each first earning its own passes. Gold items catch rubber-stamp jurors, so junk sold as a pearl costs the voter its seat.
